quickSummary: Simple distillation for large ΔT (>25 K). Fractional for close ΔT (<25 K). Steam distillation for steam-volatile, water-immiscible liquids (boils <100°C). Vacuum distillation for heat-sensitive liquids (Glycerol). TLC R_f = distance of solute / distance of solvent.
summary: Master organic purification techniques: distillation variants, sublimation, and adsorption/partition chromatography.

summaryBox.title: Distillation Selection
summaryBox.takeaway: Simple (ΔT > 25 K), Fractional (ΔT < 25 K), Steam (steam-volatile + water-immiscible, boils <100°C), Vacuum (decomposes near normal BP, e.g., Glycerol).

conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Simple Distillation**: Used for liquids with non-volatile impurities or mixtures with **large boiling point differences ($\Delta T_{\text{bp}} > 25\text{ K}$)** (*e.g., Ether $34^\circ\text{C}$ and Toluene $111^\circ\text{C}$*).
2. **Fractional Distillation**: Used for liquid mixtures with **close boiling points ($\Delta T_{\text{bp}} < 25\text{ K}$)** using fractionating columns (*e.g., Crude oil fractions, Acetone $56^\circ\text{C}$ and Methanol $65^\circ\text{C}$*).
3. **Steam Distillation**: Used for substances that are **steam-volatile and completely immiscible with water**. Since $P_{\text{total}} = P^\circ_{\text{water}} + P^\circ_{\text{organic}} = 1\text{ atm}$, the mixture **boils at a temperature BELOW $100^\circ\text{C}$** (*e.g., Aniline, Nitrobenzene, Essential oils*).
4. **Vacuum Distillation (Reduced Pressure)**: Used for liquids that decompose **at or below their normal boiling points** (*e.g., Glycerol decomposes at $290^\circ\text{C}$; distills safely at $180^\circ\text{C}$ under $12\text{ mmHg}$*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Chromatographic Separations & R_f Calculation
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Chromatographic Separations & R_f Calculation
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
RETARDATION FACTOR (R_f)

   R_f = (Distance travelled by the substance from baseline) / (Distance travelled by the solvent front from baseline)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Adsorption Chromatography (TLC / Column)**: Based on differential adsorption on a stationary solid adsorbent (Silica gel / Alumina). Components with higher affinity for adsorbent travel slower (lower $R_f$).
• **Partition Chromatography (Paper)**: Based on continuous differential partitioning of solutes between water trapped in paper fibers (stationary phase) and a mobile solvent phase.

quickRevision: In steam distillation, the mixture boils below 100°C because P_total = P_water + P_organic = 1 atm.
Glycerol is purified by vacuum distillation (distillation under reduced pressure).
Fractional distillation is mandatory when boiling points differ by less than 25 K.
keyFormulae: R_f = \frac{\text{Distance travelled by substance}}{\text{Distance travelled by solvent front}}
